archetype.name: Retooling (derailed by QB injuries)
archetype.definition: A first-year-coach team with a proven core whose season fell apart once Lamar Jackson's thumb put four different quarterbacks under center, and whose defense has slid from elite to ordinary over two years.

report.headline: A Jackson-less QB carousel exposed a defense that no longer stops big plays
report.take:
Baltimore is 4-7 in Jesse Minter's first year, last in an AFC North that Cincinnati leads at 7-3, and the record is close to honest. The point differential of -52 implies about five wins (4.8), and wins over expected sit at -0.83. This is not a good team losing coin flips. It is a middling one (net EPA 20th, offense 19th, defense 18th) that has started Jackson, Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano and Jacoby Brissett at quarterback and has not won since Week 5.

The one constant is the run game. Derrick Henry has 198 carries, the team averages 4.4 yards a carry (7th) and gets 2.6 yards before contact (10th), so the line can move people on early downs. The trouble is everything after that. Pass protection ranks 29th in pressure rate allowed, short-yardage conversion ranks dead last, and the line draws 4.3 penalties a game (29th). That leaves backup quarterbacks facing third-and-long behind a leaky front, and the turnovers follow: 17 giveaways and a -7 turnover differential. The bad games line up with quarterback trouble. Jackson's Week 8 return in Buffalo produced -18.1 passing EPA and three turnovers. Fagnano threw for 57 yards against Jacksonville. Brissett moved the ball at Carolina but gave it away four times in a two-point loss. Special teams at 27th in EPA keep leaking a little more.

The yardage numbers flatter the defense. Baltimore is 10th in passing yards allowed and 6th in EPA on short throws, so it tackles the underneath stuff. But it is 30th in EPA on deep passes and 31st in EPA per target to opposing WR1s, and 21st in red-zone touchdown rate. That adds up to 26.2 points allowed a game (25th). This is not a new-coach blip: the defense also ranked 18th in EPA allowed in 2025, after a run of top-10 units. Minter's fingerprint shows more on fourth down, where Baltimore goes for it more than anyone, than on a defense that still gives up the big play.

From here the season is about whether Jackson comes back. The Ravens think there is a chance he returns for Week 16 against Cleveland. Until then, Henry and a game-manager quarterback are the plan, against a closing schedule of five division and winning-record opponents plus a Tampa defense ranked 3rd. The upside is spoiling someone's season, not chasing a playoff spot.

strengths.title: Henry and a road-grading run game
strengths.body: Henry has carried the offense regardless of who plays quarterback, and the line gives him real room before contact. Run blocking is the line's one top-10 trait, and it gives a backup quarterback a game plan. It should hold, though a 22% stuff rate and the worst short-yardage conversion rate in the league show it bogs down when defenses know it's coming.

strengths.title: Short passes and goal-line runs contained
strengths.body: Baltimore tackles well enough underneath that short throws are a losing proposition for opponents, and it allows few rushing touchdowns. That is why the yardage totals look respectable. It is a real skill of this unit, but it only covers half the field.

strengths.title: Aggressive fourth-down decisions
strengths.body: Minter's staff goes for it on fourth down more than anyone. That is sound process for an offense that runs well and a team that needs to steal points. The catch is a line that ranks last in short-yardage conversion, so the payoff depends on how the line holds up in those spots.

concerns.title: Defense gets beaten deep
concerns.body: The underneath coverage is good, but the deep game and opposing top receivers carve it up. That is why points allowed run far worse than yards allowed. With safety Jaylinn Hawkins out and Marlon Humphrey's status unclear, the problem gets worse before it gets better. Because 2025 looked similar, this looks like a real flaw rather than noise.

concerns.title: Protection collapses behind backup QBs
concerns.body: Baltimore allows pressure at one of the league's highest rates and draws line penalties constantly. Jackson can escape that pressure; Huntley, Fagnano and Brissett mostly have not. This is a line flaw that the quarterback injury exposed rather than one it caused, so it lasts at least until Jackson is back.

concerns.title: Turnovers and special teams leaks
concerns.body: Seventeen giveaways against ten takeaways means Baltimore keeps handing over field position, and special teams rank 27th in EPA on top of that. Some of the turnover damage is quarterback-specific, since the Carolina and Jacksonville games had multiple giveaways with backups. Expect it to ease only somewhat.

trend.note: A strong September with Jackson gave way to a slide with no wins since Week 5, including blowouts by Cincinnati, Buffalo and Jacksonville. The last two were one-score losses, and the offense showed life at Carolina, but four giveaways sank that one.

nextGame.headline: Henry's ground game against Stroud's arm, with Baltimore's secondary depleted
nextGame.body:
Houston is 4-6, but it is better than that. It has a positive point differential (+2.1 a game), wins over expected of -1.82 (30th), and has won only 20% of its one-score games. C.J. Stroud has started every week behind a line that allows pressure at the 4th-lowest rate, and the passing offense ranks 8th in EPA. The Texans' run game is poor (3.32 yards a carry, 25th), which is why they pass more than expected. Their defense leads the league in sacks with 29 and ranks 6th in success rate allowed, but it gives up explosive passes at the second-worst rate in the league. The Book has Houston by 6.5 with a total of 46.5, and Baltimore is +251 on the moneyline.

Availability cuts both ways. Baltimore is without Jackson (IR), safety Jaylinn Hawkins and DT Nnamdi Madubuike, and Marlon Humphrey is listed out as a coach's decision even though he is back at the facility. That is three of the defense's most-used players, most of them in the pass defense Stroud will attack. Houston will be without edge Danielle Hunter, WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and G Wyatt Teller. G Keylan Rutledge, DT Sheldon Rankins and WR Kayshon Boutte are questionable, and RB Woody Marks (concussion) is trending toward playing. Losing Hunter matters most for Baltimore's shaky protection.

waysToWin.title: Lean on Henry, shorten the game
waysToWin.body: Houston is middling against the run, and Baltimore's line run-blocks well. Long Henry drives keep Stroud on the sideline and protect whichever quarterback starts. It also limits the dropbacks that feed Houston's league-leading sack total.

waysToWin.title: Take the shots Houston gives up
waysToWin.body: Houston's defense wins on early downs but gets hit for explosive passes, and opposing WR2s have scored well above their norm against it. Play-action off the Henry looks to Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman can produce the chunk plays that change a game. Mark Andrews faces a tougher draw, since Houston is stingy against tight ends.

waysToWin.title: Keep it close, test Houston late
waysToWin.body: Houston has been bad in close games all year, and Baltimore covered and nearly won its last game. If the run game and fourth-down aggression keep this within a score into the fourth quarter, the Texans' late-game issues become Baltimore's best chance.

waysToLose.title: Stroud picks apart a thin secondary
waysToLose.body: Baltimore's worst trait, deep coverage, meets an efficient passer with clean pockets. The Ravens are also missing a starting safety and possibly Humphrey. Two or three big completions can decide it before Henry's volume matters.

waysToLose.title: Pass rush overwhelms the protection
waysToLose.body: Even without Hunter, Houston gets sacks at the 3rd-best rate. Baltimore allows pressure at the 29th rate, so a few early incompletions or a deficit that forces passing can turn this into a sack-and-giveaway day for a backup quarterback.

waysToLose.title: Giveaways hand over short fields
waysToLose.body: Baltimore has multiple turnovers in four games, including four at Carolina last week. A defense already 25th in points allowed cannot absorb short fields against an offense ranked 8th in EPA.

nextGame.watch: How Baltimore covers Stroud's first deep shot without Hawkins and possibly Humphrey: if those throws land, the Henry plan never gets to work.

restOfSeason.body:
The run game and the underneath defense are real and should hold, so Baltimore stays competitive in most weeks. But the deep-ball defense, the pass protection and the turnover habit are structural rather than unlucky, and the record already tracks the point differential. With no luck to regress toward, there is no hidden rebound in the numbers. The schedule offers little relief: Tampa's defense ranks 3rd, and the closing run is Pittsburgh twice, Cleveland and Cincinnati, all with winning records.

The swing is Jackson. If he returns for Week 16 even close to healthy, the offense jumps back toward the efficient group that scored 41 in Week 1, and Baltimore can spoil a division rival's season. If he doesn't, expect more of the Huntley/Brissett pattern: enough rushing to hang around and enough mistakes to lose. A losing season looks likely either way.

confidence.note: Eleven games of data, but four QBs and an uncertain Jackson return blur the real level.
